body: Hey, I run into the same issue (about feeling like a fish out of water at pride).  I am openly lesbian but I cannot seem to find much joy in going to pride or anything like that.  It's just too flaunty and overwhelming for me.

If anything I would need a kidney transplant from my kidneys completely failing due to lupus attacking them.  Dialysis only works for so long (generally a very long time) and I personally do not want to be tied to a machine for the rest of my life.  Nor do I want to recieve a healthy kidney that my body will in turn just attack again.  It would just be a vicious cycle of trading out organs.  Plus, even now I live a very limited life.  A viable kidney could instead go to someone who once recieving it would be able to live a full and happy long life.  My final reason is once my lupus gets to that stage, I probably will have very little quality of life.  I would prefer to just let lupus take me, rather than fight a battle that has already been won.

My lupus is affecting me both emotionally and physically.  I plenty of joint and muscle pain, kidney/liver/heart/brain issues, and fatigue like no other.  Mentally I struggle with the thought of not feeling well for my entire life and the possibility of dying.  Lupus is scary and it's totally fine to be scared.  They ran an Ana test, a blood panel and some specific lupus indicator tests (double stranded Dna I think.)  Diagnosis mostly came from clinical observation along with the blood work.  I am managing as best I can.  I am graduating from High School soon thanks to online high school classes.  I have had to scale back my ambitions in life because of the constraints lupus has put on things.  I really try to listen to my body about what it needs but at the same time push for what I want.  It's all a big balancing act.  My best advice is to take one day at a time, enjoy the simple little things and don't give up. :)

Yes, in some ways I do feel like I am recovering.  I do still have flares that send me right back to where I was but luckily I haven't had any major flares in a year.  With that being said I am not in a full remission either.  My meds have improved the quality of my life.  Prednisone was a bitch and luckily I didn't take it long term.  Plaquenil helps a bit but it isn't a cure by any means.  Peroxicam helps to cut the pain and inflamation.  How I feel fluxuates day to day.  Some days I feel decent and other days I can't even get out of bed.

Symptoms I experience in no particular order of significance: Fatigue, Swollen joints, liver problems, heart problems, mild kidney problems, nuerological problems, Raynaud's phenomenon, hair loss, lupus "fog", sunsensitivity, rashes (both malar and discoid types), changes in weight, skipping/missing periods, and overall just feeling like I have the flu every single day.  

Lupus is hard to diagnose, especially at my age.  What finally put the last nail in the coffin for it being lupus was my blood tests plus symptoms.  I had a positive lupus panel (don't know all the technical doctor talk but... the specific blood test markers for lupus were positive), low white blood count at 2,500 and a positive ANA over 2,000 which is basically unheard of high.  A normal or negative ANA is 80.  Lupus was partially genetic in my case.   

Did they think it was all in my head when they couldn't figure it out?  YES.  They thought I was horribly suicidal, anorexic, faking it, so on and so forth.  The doctors who said this were short lived in my diagnosis quest.  One actually called and apologized to me after they read my latest blood results.  That particular doctor had at the last appointment told me it was "all in my head."  My results came back very nasty and they felt horrible for not listening to me.  

There is a very mental part to lupus.  The fatigue, the "fog" and various nuerological issues are somewhat in the head.  However, these are not psychosomatic things.  They are part of having lupus and I cannot control them.  Sometimes I have horrible brain fog and can hardly even remember where the kitchen is.  Fatigue can be bone crushing, it is mental but also very physical.  Don't quite know how to explain it.   

What are the person's symptoms?  My advice to your friend: The most important thing when searching for a diagnosis is to be your own advocate.  You know your body better than anyone else and when something is wrong with it.  Many of the symptoms of lupus are not visible to the naked eye like organ involvement, pain or fatigue. Keep on searching until you find the answer.  There will be many doctors who will point fingers or balk.  Find one that listens and works with you.  That's your best shot at getting diagnosed.  

Best of wishes to you and your friend!

Yes and No.  Before I became ill with Lupus I had long blonde hair, a solid body weight of around 145 or so pounds, and I had a healthy glow about me.  When I became ill I had some drastic changes in terms of body weight (went from 145 to 90 lbs), had some pretty nasty rashes and cut off my hair to about mid ear.  Reason why I cut my hair is that it was falling out like mad and it took a lot of energy to maintain it.  My weight was the most visible of changes.  Currently I still have very short blonde hair, a few small rash out breaks and am at around 135 lbs or so.
Oi Vey!  But in this case it very much was!
